dataFlow: A shopper on a sold-out product page submits their email through the widget, which records a waitlist subscription scoped to a specific variant or to the whole product; duplicate signups for the same item and email are a no-op. When stock returns, an inventory-level-changed event resolves the affected item, and if availability crossed from zero to positive a restock event is recorded once per item. A recurring job processes pending restock events during the merchant's quiet-hours window: it loads the waiting subscribers in signup order, allocates only as many notifications as units returned, emails the front of the queue with a rendered template and one-click unsubscribe link, and leaves the rest queued for the next restock — recording one notification per subscriber per restock so brief stock dips never double-send. When an order is created, line items are matched against notified subscribers within a seven-day window to credit recovered purchases. Deleted products cascade-clear their waitlists, and the admin dashboard ranks products by waitlist size with drill-in, CSV export, template and quiet-hours settings, and a lost-demand-recovered metric.

edgeCases: Duplicate inventory-level webhook delivery for the same item — only record a restock when availability crosses zero-to-positive and suppress when an unprocessed restock event already exists, so brief dips never re-trigger.
Duplicate order-created or product-delete webhook delivery — purchase crediting is keyed by order and notification, and cascade-clear is a no-op when no subscriptions remain.
Partial restock with many waiting — notify only as many front-of-queue subscribers in signup order as units returned, leaving the rest queued for the next restock.
Same email signs up for the same variant twice — no-op via the natural-identity key; the same email across different products or scopes creates distinct queues.

Back-in-stock email bounces or the email provider fails — record the notification as bounced or failed with the reason and exclude it from the notified count, never silently retrying into a duplicate blast.
Quiet hours straddle midnight in the merchant's timezone — the job evaluates the window timezone-aware and defers all sends until the window reopens.
Variant cannot be resolved from the inventory item id (item already deleted) — skip recording the restock rather than emailing about a missing product.
